summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet assured that the Cambodian government will mobilize the national budget and partner assistance to protect and restore infrastructure for internally displaced people (IDPs) affected by the border conflict. Meanwhile, at the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat in Cebu, Cambodia's top diplomat briefed counterparts on the border situation, emphasizing a commitment to peaceful resolution in accordance with international law.
title: Cambodian PM pledges support for IDPs; ASEAN ministers discuss border de-escalation

summary: The Royal Thai Air Force (RTAF) has maintained constant surveillance and readiness since the December 27 ceasefire. Air Marshal Chakkrit Thammavichai stated that there have been 2-3 provocations from the Cambodian side, including an incident where a flare device on the border fence was triggered. The RTAF maintains its operations are based on self-defense and humanitarian principles, and that it is prepared to sustain operations for the next 2-3 years if necessary.
title: Air Force says Thai forces on standby after repeated provocations

summary: A tour of the O'Smach Resort scam compound shows it is now under Thai military control following the December conflict. Evidence found inside includes mock police stations and uniforms from seven different countries used to facilitate international fraud operations.
title: Video shows former scam operation at Thai-Cambodia border

summary: Cambodia's Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) has sent a formal note verbale to Thailand proposing that joint survey teams return to the field between February 9 and 13, 2026. The Cambodian side also issued a strong protest against Thai military units, alleging the destruction of homes and property belonging to Cambodian citizens and the prevention of their return to border areas. Cambodia stated it would not recognize any border alterations resulting from the use of force.
title: Cambodia presses Thailand to act on stalled border demarcation, protests military actions

summary: At a UN Security Council meeting in New York, Cambodian Ambassador Keo Chhea and Thai representative Cherdchai Chaivaivid exchanged legal arguments over treaty compliance. Cambodia accused Thailand of undermining legal certainties, while Thailand rejected 'selective' application of international law. The exchange follows two major military clashes in July and December 2025.
title: Cambodia and Thailand spar again on the global stage over border dispute

summary: Associated Press reporters visited a captured scam compound in O'Smach, Cambodia, now occupied by Thai troops. The site features high-tech infrastructure, including rooms set up to look like Chinese police stations used to intimidate victims. The Thai military claims the facility was used as a base by Cambodian forces during the December conflict.
title: Images Show Abandoned Belongings and Mock Police Stations at a Former Scam Center in Asia

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow warned Cambodia against escalation after an incident last Friday night at Phu Pha Lek. Cambodian troops reportedly triggered a flare alarm, leading to a Thai warning shell and a subsequent M79 grenade explosion. The standoff occurs just days before Thailand's general election scheduled for February 8.
title: Thailand urges Cambodia to avoid provocative acts

summary: Thai military officials invited foreign delegates and reporters to the O'Smach border complex to view evidence of transnational fraud. The complex, seized during late 2025 clashes, allegedly housed human trafficking victims forced to conduct scams. Documents and scripts were found in a bombed six-story building. Cambodia’s Interior Ministry dismissed the display as a 'pretext' for military aggression.
title: Cambodian scam compound yields trove of fraud evidence, Thai military says

summary: Phnom Penh will host top leaders from Vietnam and Laos on February 6-7, 2026. While officially focused on trilateral cooperation and sovereignty, political analysts suggest the meeting could be a strategic move to strengthen regional alliances amid the ongoing border standoff with Thailand. The meeting aims to foster 'mutual respect for independence' and security cooperation across the three neighboring nations.
title: Cambodia to Host Vietnam-Laos Leaders as Analyst Sees Potential Impact on Thailand Tensions

summary: An assessment by the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) highlights the severe economic fallout from the 2025 border clashes. Prolonged closures of 6 major crossings and 10 checkpoints have disrupted trade, tourism, and remittances from 1.2 million Cambodian workers in Thailand. The report warns that if clashes renew, Cambodia’s GDP growth could fall below 4% in 2026.
title: Economic Shockwaves from Cambodia–Thailand Border Conflict Threaten 2026 Growth

summary: The Regional Border Committee (RBC) secretariat meeting between Cambodia's Military Region 3 and Thailand's Chanthaburi-Trat Border Defence Command took place at the Cham Yeam–Hat Lek crossing. Monitored by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), the meeting ended without a consensus on border issues. Both sides agreed to return to headquarters for further document exchanges but reaffirmed their commitment to the December ceasefire and regional stability.
title: Cambodia–Thailand RBC holds special meeting in Koh Kong under AOT

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a strong protest against Thailand on February 4 regarding an 'unauthorized field visit' conducted on February 2. Led by the Chief of Thai Army Intelligence, a group of foreign military attachés and law enforcement officials visited two hotels in the O Smach district, which Cambodia claims is a violation of its sovereignty. Cambodia alleges the area was occupied by force during Thai military offensives in December 2025.
title: Cambodia Slams Thai Military-Led “Field Visit” to Hotels in Occupied O Smach District

summary: A missionary in Cambodia reports that thousands of refugees remain displaced in border provinces, facing extreme suffering and precarious living conditions. While the military conflict has largely shifted to social media, the land border remains closed, forcing travelers to detour through Laos or fly. Diplomatic efforts are described as stalled as both nations await the outcome of the February 8 Thai elections to see if a new administration will pursue peace.
title: ASIA/CAMBODIA - A missionary: “Tension and hostility with Thailand persist, while the battle rages on social media”

summary: As of late January 2026, over 141,000 people remain displaced due to the border conflict that escalated in late 2025. While many have returned following the December 27 ceasefire, significant humanitarian needs persist in shelter, health, and food security. Border crossings remain largely closed, severely impacting local livelihoods and trade.
title: WeWorld Flash Update #1 – Escalating crisis along the Cambodia - Thailand border

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has formally requested historical and technical documents from France to resolve the ongoing border dispute. This follows two major military escalations in 2025 that killed a total of 144 people and displaced over half a million. The current border is based on maps drawn by France in 1907.
title: Cambodia asks France to provide historical evidence to help settle Thai border dispute

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has formally requested historical and technical documents from France, specifically maps from the 1907 colonial era, to clarify territorial claims. The move follows two major military escalations in 2025 that resulted in approximately 101 deaths and massive displacement. France has reportedly expressed willingness to assist in the mediation.
title: Cambodia Seeks French Historical Records to Resolve Thai Border Dispute

summary: A 40mm grenade was reportedly fired from the Cambodian side at approximately 10:18 a.m. on Thursday, landing at a military base in Thailand's Sisaket Province. According to Thailand's Second Army Region, there were no casualties reported from the incident.
title: Cambodia fires grenade into Thai territory: Thai media

summary: A special session of the Thai-Cambodian Regional Border Committee (RBC) held in Thailand's Trat province concluded without a joint summary or agreement. While Thailand aimed to maintain communication and reduce field tensions, Cambodia reportedly introduced border demarcation proposals that Thailand deemed outside the committee's scope. ASEAN monitoring teams were present as observers.
title: Thai-Cambodian border meeting ends without agreement

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has formally requested historical documents and expert advice from France to help settle the border dispute with Thailand. The request follows two major outbreaks of armed conflict in 2025 that killed over 140 people and displaced hundreds of thousands. The 817-km border was originally mapped by France in 1907.
title: Cambodia turns to France for historical documents to resolve Thai border clashes

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has requested historical documents from French President Emmanuel Macron to help resolve the border dispute. This follows two major military clashes in July and December 2025 that killed over 100 people and displaced half a million. Cambodia is looking to internationalize the legal basis of the border using the 1907 Franco-Siamese Treaty.
title: Cambodia asks France to provide historical evidence to help settle Thailand border dispute

summary: The Thai army's Second Army Region reported that a 40mm grenade was fired from the Cambodian side on Thursday morning, landing near a Thai operational base in Sisaket Province. There were no reported casualties. Cambodian authorities have denied the claim.
title: Xinhua Asia-Pacific news summary: Grenade reported in Sisaket

summary: As of early February 2026, nearly 98,000 people remain displaced due to the conflict that began in late 2025. While 85% of the original 640,000 displaced persons have returned, those remaining face acute needs in health, education, and shelter, with 48 schools still closed.
title: World Vision Situation Report #23: Displacement Crisis as a Result of the Cambodia–Thailand Border Conflict

summary: The ongoing border dispute with Cambodia is reportedly eroding support for the Pheu Thai party in its traditional stronghold of northeast Thailand ahead of Sunday's elections. Voters in border provinces like Sa Kaeo expressed anger over the perceived loss of national honor and the economic impact of closed border crossings. Meanwhile, nationalist rhetoric from rival parties promising border walls and military recruitment is gaining traction among displaced residents.
title: Border conflict weakens Thailand's Thaksin in heartland

summary: As the Philippines assumes the 2026 ASEAN chairmanship, the border dispute between Thailand and Cambodia is seen as a major test of the bloc's internal cohesion. The conflict, involving heavy artillery and F-16 airstrikes in late 2025, resulted in nearly one million people displaced at its peak. Analysts suggest the dispute undermines ASEAN's image as a peace-promoting bloc.
title: Philippines Takes ASEAN Chair as Cambodia-Thailand Border Tensions Test Bloc’s Conflict-Management Role

summary: AFP journalists were the first international media to access the 11th-century Preah Vihear temple since the December 2025 ceasefire. They documented significant damage, including shrapnel scars and broken sandstone, which Cambodian officials attribute to Thai artillery and aerial strikes. Over 560 parts of the complex were reportedly damaged across two rounds of fighting last year. Thailand has previously claimed Cambodia used the temple as a military outpost, voiding its protected status.
title: Cambodia reveals damage to UNESCO-listed temple after Thailand clashes

summary: Thai military officials state they have secured key defensive positions along the K5 border road for 56 days since December 22. While large-scale fighting has subsided, troops continue to clear landmines and unexploded ordnance daily in disputed areas near Boundary Marker No. 36.
title: Border standoff eases on K5, but mines and bombs still found daily

summary: Journalists visited the 'Royal Hill' scam compound near the border, which was bombed by the Thai military during the December conflict. The site is now occupied by Thai forces, revealing documents and setups used for industrial-scale global fraud.
title: Scammers' abandoned Cambodia compound exposes brutality and banality of fraud

summary: Thais head to the polls today in a general election defined by the border conflict with Cambodia. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul called the snap election in December following the ouster of Paetongtarn Shinawatra. Analysts suggest the timing was intended to capitalize on surging nationalism fueled by the military clashes.
title: Thailand votes in three-way race as risk of instability looms

summary: Thailand held a general election on February 8, 2026, characterized by high nationalist sentiment following last year's border clashes. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, who took office after Paetongtarn Shinawatra was removed for alleged mishandling of relations with Cambodia, has positioned his party as the defender of Thai sovereignty. The conflict has significantly influenced voter priorities and the political standing of the military.
title: Thailand counts votes in early election with 3 main parties vying for power

summary: The Bhumjaithai Party, led by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, won a decisive victory in the February 8 general election. Reuters and Bloomberg report that Anutin successfully leveraged nationalist sentiment surrounding the border conflict with Cambodia to gain rural support. Analysts suggest the election results may signal a continued hardline stance on territorial disputes, as the pro-reform People's Party moves to the opposition.
title: Foreign media: Anutin's nationalist bet delivers landslide

summary: Unofficial results from Thailand’s February 8 general election show the conservative Bhumjaithai Party, led by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, taking a commanding lead with approximately 194 seats. The election was heavily influenced by the border conflict, with Bhumjaithai adopting a hawkish stance to garner nationalist support. Despite the lead, the party lacks a simple majority (251 seats) and must seek coalition partners, likely the Pheu Thai party, to form a stable government.
title: Thailand’s Conservative Bhumjaithai Party Tops Polls but Will Need Partners To Form Government

summary: Thai security officials report a concerning military build-up on the Cambodian side of the border. Intelligence suggests Cambodia has acquired sophisticated anti-aircraft systems to counter Thailand's air superiority. Officials warned that tensions have reached a flashpoint and hostilites could erupt at any moment, particularly as the political landscape shifts following the Thai general election.
title: Thai security officials warn of renewed conflict with Cambodia

summary: On February 8, the Cambodian government spokesperson Pen Bona condemned recent Thai military actions, including the placement of shipping containers and barbed wire in disputed areas. Cambodia argues these moves violate the December 27 Joint Border Committee agreement and prevent civilians from accessing their property. This follows accusations earlier in the week regarding 'erroneous shooting' and illegal territory control.
title: Cambodia condemns Thailand's move along the border

summary: International news agencies report that Thai security officials issued a 'stark warning' regarding a concerning escalation of military activity. Intelligence suggests Cambodian forces may be preparing for a new wave of strikes, despite the December ceasefire.
title: Thai security officials warn of renewed conflict with Cambodia, citing border military build-up

summary: Thai security officials have issued warnings of a 'concerning' escalation of military activity on the Cambodian side. Intelligence suggests Phnom Penh is acquiring sophisticated anti-aircraft systems to neutralize Thai air superiority. The border is designated a critical security vulnerability following the February 8 election.
title: Thailand on high alert as security chiefs warn of renewed border conflict

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's Bhumjaithai Party secured approximately 192 seats in Sunday's snap election, a victory analysts attribute to his 'wartime leader' image during the late 2025 border conflict with Cambodia. Anutin had dissolved parliament in December amid the crisis. The election results suggest a shift toward a more stable but nationalist-leaning government, which may lead to the scrapping of maritime energy agreements with Cambodia while maintaining a hardline military stance on land border disputes.
title: Thailand PM Anutin powers to emphatic election win

summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, following his Bhumjaithai Party's victory in the February 8 election, has instructed agencies to prepare for the cancellation of MOU 44. This 2001 agreement provided a framework for maritime boundary and resource-sharing negotiations. Anutin cited a lack of progress over 25 years and domestic political pressure following deadly border clashes as reasons for the move.
title: Thailand to cancel MOU 44 with Cambodia, says PM Anutin

summary: Analysts suggest that the victory of the Bhumjaithai Party in the February 8 Thai elections may lead to continued border tensions. The party's campaign included nationalist rhetoric and promises to reinforce border security with permanent fencing, which could hinder swift diplomatic resolution.
title: Will Thailand’s New Government Change Its Relationship with Cambodia?

summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has instructed officials to prepare to void 'MoU 44,' a 25-year-old agreement intended to resolve overlapping maritime claims. Following his party's success in the February 8 election, Anutin cited a lack of progress as the reason for scrapping the deal. This move signals a more hardline approach to territorial disputes with Cambodia under the incoming Thai government.
title: Thailand ready to scrap sea-boundary deal with Cambodia

summary: A humanitarian crisis is unfolding along the border as thousands of foreign workers flee scam compounds in areas like O'Smach following military strikes and increased pressure. Shelters are overwhelmed due to a lack of state support and the previous dismantling of USAID in the region.
title: In Cambodia, thousands flood out of 'scam compounds' and find increasingly little help

summary: Cambodian authorities have shut down 190 scam centers following intense international pressure and border friction with Thailand. Reuters reports that one site at the Chong Chom-O'Smach border crossing was previously bombed and occupied by the Thai military in December. The conflict was significantly driven by Thai operations targeting these criminal networks situated in disputed territory.
title: Cambodia says it has closed almost 200 scam centers in fraud crackdown

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., chief of staff of the Philippines armed forces, met with Cambodian PM Hun Manet in Phnom Penh on Thursday. As the current ASEAN chair, the Philippines confirmed it is closely monitoring the situation and will lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to maintain peace. Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to a peaceful resolution based on international law and the December 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: Asean chair Philippines monitoring border issue, AOT will continue to facilitate resolution

summary: The Philippine Armed Forces Chief, General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., visited the Cambodia-Thailand border to monitor the situation. The visit signals the Philippines' active role as the 2026 ASEAN Chair in leading the ASEAN Observers Team (AOT) to mediate the dispute.
title: ASEAN Chair Philippines Inspects Banteay Meanchey Border

summary: A landmine explosion on February 11 in Thailand's Si Sa Ket province wounded three Thai soldiers, with one losing a leg. The incident occurred while the soldiers were surveying the border. This blast marks a significant disruption to the relative calm established by the December 27 ceasefire following months of deadly clashes.
title: New landmine blast tests Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire

summary: Thailand's consumer confidence index rose to 52.8 in January from 51.9 in December. The University of the Thai Chamber of Commerce attributed this rise partly to the easing of border tensions with Cambodia and expectations surrounding the new government following the February general election.
title: Thailand's consumer confidence picks up in January

summary: Scholars from China, Cambodia, and Thailand met in Beijing on February 10 to advance the 'Fuxian consensus' reached in late 2025. The dialogue focused on restoring trust, which remains fragile due to legal disputes and nationalism. The experts proposed resuming bilateral exchanges and using the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation mechanism to stabilize the ceasefire.
title: Track II Diplomacy in Action: Scholars Forge Pathways for Cambodia-Thailand Peace

summary: International observers are pressuring both Thailand and Cambodia to uphold the fragile ceasefire as over 79,000 displaced residents remain unable to return home. Reports from Banteay Meanchey province indicate that Thai personnel have demolished some civilian infrastructure in the Boeng Trakuon area. The Cambodian government is urging the UN and ASEAN to monitor what it describes as continued 'military occupation' by Thai forces despite the halt in active fighting.
title: Cambodia-Thailand border remains under international scrutiny

summary: Following the February 8 elections in Thailand, religious leaders are calling on the winning Bhumjaithai Party to prioritize a lasting peace deal. Reports indicate that the conflict has caused at least 18 civilian deaths in Cambodia and left 79 others injured as of late 2025.
title: Thai Bishop Calls on Newly Elected Government to Promote Lasting Peace with Cambodia

summary: The Philippines has formally begun its leadership of the ASEAN Observers Team (AOT), taking over from Malaysia. Gen. Romeo S. Brawner Jr., Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, arrived for a four-day mission to assess border conditions in Banteay Meanchey. The transition is seen as a critical step in ensuring the implementation of the December 27 Joint Statement, with the Philippines pledging an impartial approach to de-escalate ongoing tensions.
title: ASEAN Steps Up Mediation in Cambodia-Thailand Border Dispute as Philippines Takes Lead

summary: Six weeks after the December 27 ceasefire, thousands of Cambodians remain in temporary shelters. Reuters reports that the Thai military has installed metal shipping containers and barbed wire at Ban Nong Ya Kaew (known as Prey Chan in Cambodia). While Thailand claims these barriers are for 'safety and security' consistent with the truce, Cambodian officials state 80% of homes in the area remain inaccessible. Recent landmine incidents continue to cause casualties, with a Thai soldier losing a leg on Feb 11.
title: Displaced Cambodians in limbo near contested border

summary: Following an election victory, the new Thai government under Anutin Charnvirakul has taken a hardline stance on maritime sovereignty. The Royal Thai Navy recently intercepted 25 Cambodian fishing boats near Koh Kut. Thailand has also moved to suspend existing maritime border negotiations and 'MoU 44,' while increasing defense spending for border security.
title: New Thai Government Asserts Control over Coastal Waters

summary: The Philippines, as the 2026 ASEAN Chair, is facing its first major diplomatic test with the renewed frictions on the Cambodia-Thailand border. Analysts suggest that Manila will need to perform a delicate balancing act to maintain ASEAN centrality while navigating the involvement of major powers like the U.S. and China in the peace process.
title: Regional Flashpoints Set To Test Philippines Leadership As ASEAN Chair

summary: In his first interview with international media, PM Hun Manet alleged that Thai forces remain positioned deep within Cambodian territory despite the December 27 ceasefire. Speaking in Washington, he claimed Thai troops have used shipping containers and barbed wire to block roads, preventing 80,000 displaced Cambodians from returning home. He called for the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to resume work now that Thailand's elections are over. Thailand has denied occupying territory, stating it is maintaining positions for de-escalation.
title: Exclusive: Cambodian PM says Thailand is occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: During a visit to Washington for the 'Board of Peace' meeting, PM Hun Manet told Reuters that Thai forces are occupying territory deep within Cambodian lines, beyond Thailand's own unilateral claims. He cited the use of shipping containers and barbed wire to block roads. Thailand denies these claims, stating it is maintaining positions for de-escalation. Manet urged the Joint Boundary Commission to begin work now that Thailand's February 8 election is over.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: The analysis highlights that the border conflict has entered a dangerous phase where domestic political pressures in both Bangkok and Phnom Penh outweigh international mediation. Following the February 8 Thai general election, nationalist sentiments have risen. The report suggests that while a ceasefire is in place, military objectives in Bangkok and the vulnerabilities of Cambodia's forward defenses create a risk of a long-term contest rather than a permanent peace.
title: Thailand-Cambodia conflict: The trap of a long war

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has accused Thailand of maintaining military positions deep within Cambodian territory despite the December 27 ceasefire. Speaking from Washington, he described the border situation as 'fragile' and called for the resumption of the Joint Boundary Commission. He suggested that U.S. President Donald Trump's new 'Board of Peace' could assist in de-escalation.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand occupying 'deep' territory after ceasefire

summary: Border tensions spiked on February 16, 2026, as Thai authorities reported increased military movements from Cambodia near Ubon Ratchathani, involving an estimated 10,000 soldiers. Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow is shifting the diplomatic narrative by highlighting Cambodia-based online scams at the UN Human Rights Council (Feb 23-25) to counter Cambodia's territorial accusations.
title: Thailand and Cambodia's diplomatic rivalry intensifies as online scams add complexity to border tensions

summary: Reports indicate that Thai soldiers and media recently visited areas near Sadok Kok Thom Historical Park as tensions remain high. PM Hun Manet alleged that Thailand's recent election, which saw the victory of PM Anutin Charnvirakul, involved 'heightened nationalist rhetoric' that has delayed technical boundary work.
title: Thailand still 'occupying' territory after ceasefire, Cambodia PM says

summary: The Royal Thai Army spokesperson, Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree, rejected accusations made by Hun Manet. Thailand claims the area in question is Thai territory where Cambodian civilians and soldiers encroached over time after being sheltered during past wars. The spokesperson stated these individuals are not 'displaced persons' but are violating Thai sovereignty, and the use of barriers is a lawful measure to secure Thai territory.
title: Thailand rejects Cambodian PM's border occupation claims

summary: In an exclusive interview with Reuters while visiting Washington D.C., Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Thai forces are occupying territory 'deep' into Cambodia, beyond even Thailand's own claims. He described the situation as 'fragile' and called for the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to resume work. Thailand's Ministry of Defense denied the claims, stating they are adhering to the joint agreement to maintain existing troop deployments without further reinforcement.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand is occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: Reporting from Washington, Hun Manet urged Thailand to allow the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to begin demarcation immediately. He noted that technical work has been delayed, with Thailand citing its February 8, 2026, election as a reason for postponement. The Cambodian leader stressed that while ties with the US and China are strong, the border remains a critical flashpoint that requires international attention through the newly formed 'Board of Peace'.
title: Cambodia alleges Thailand violating territorial agreement

summary: An investigative report claims that the conflict has resulted in approximately 149 deaths and displaced 640,000 civilians. The report criticizes Thailand for rejecting multiple mediation offers from the U.S., China, and Malaysia, and alleges the use of disproportionate force, including cluster munitions in late 2025. It also highlights the link between border tensions and the crackdown on Cambodian-based scam centers.
title: How Thailand Turned a Border Dispute Into an Illegal War

summary: Recent developments highlight a shift in Cambodian diplomacy, using the 'Board of Peace' meeting to spotlight the Thai military occupation. Cambodia is reportedly planning to build 3,000 houses for displaced residents near the border, while analysts warn that ongoing conflicts and regional sanctions make ambitious trade targets between the two nations unrealistic for the 2026 fiscal year.
title: Asia Daily: February 19, 2026

summary: U.S. Deputy Secretary Landau met with PM Hun Manet in Washington to discuss the Cambodia-Thailand border situation. The U.S. commended Cambodia's participation as a founding member of the Board of Peace. The discussions also covered security cooperation and efforts to combat international online scam operations targeting Americans, which has become a secondary point of friction in the border dispute.
title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet

summary: Tourism operators in seven provinces along the Thailand-Cambodia border are appealing for government stimulus. Despite the current ceasefire, domestic and international tourism has plummeted since mid-2025 due to the conflict, leaving businesses in Ubon Ratchathani, Sisaket, and Sa Kaeo struggling.
title: Thai-Cambodian border provinces seek tourism recovery measures

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
summary: Japan's Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation, Hayashi Teiji, is scheduled to visit Thailand, Cambodia, and the Philippines (ASEAN Chair) from February 23 to 27. The mission aims to encourage the steady implementation of the December 27 ceasefire. Japan has already provided equipment to the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and is engaging in diplomatic efforts to ensure regional stability amid the fragile border situation.
title: Visit of Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation HAYASHI to Thailand, Cambodia, and the Philippines

summary: Cambodia has filed a formal protest against the Royal Thai Navy for alleged unauthorized presence in its territorial waters off Koh Kong. The incident involved the arrest of three Cambodians and the seizure of their fishing vessel approximately 7.2 nautical miles from Koh Yor. Cambodia labels this a 'clear violation' of international law and sovereignty.
title: Thai Navy Breached Cambodia's Sovereign Waters, Conducted Unauthorised Patrols

summary: The Royal Thai Army has rejected an international report claiming Thailand used excessive force, including F-16 airstrikes, to influence domestic elections in Bangkok. Army spokesperson Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree stated that operations are strictly 'legitimate self-defence' under the UN Charter and denied using the border dispute for political gain.
title: Thai army insists Cambodia border actions not politically motivated

summary: Civil society organizations released a statement noting that 170,000 civilians remain displaced and unable to return home due to military presence and infrastructure damage. The report highlights incursions in Cambodian territory and the destruction of civilian assets, urging both nations to honor the ASEAN Charter and previous ceasefire commitments.
title: Statement Calling for Legal and Peaceful Resolution of the Cambodia–Thailand Border Conflict

summary: The Thai army reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in Sisaket province on Tuesday morning. According to the Thai statement, Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol, prompting a return shot from an M79 launcher as a warning. No injuries were reported. The Thai military suggested the incident might have been caused by a rotation of new Cambodian troops unfamiliar with the area.
title: Thai army says exchanged fire with Cambodia at border

summary: Cambodia's Information Minister Neth Pheaktra dismissed Thai military claims that Cambodian soldiers fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai patrol in Sisaket province. Thailand's army reported returning fire as a warning, suggesting the incident might have been caused by new, inexperienced Cambodian troops during a rotation. Cambodia labeled the claims as 'fabricated' and intended to mislead public opinion.
title: Cambodia rejects claim its forces fired on Thai patrol

summary: Tensions remain high following a reported skirmish in the Sisaket province. While the Thai military accused Cambodia of violating the December ceasefire by firing a grenade, Phnom Penh officials have denied the use of any weapons. This flare-up is the first significant incident since the December 2025 truce, following a year of conflict that displaced over a million people.
title: Thailand, Cambodia dispute exchange of fire at border

summary: Thailand's military reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in Sisaket province on Tuesday morning. The Thai army claims Cambodian troops fired a 40mm grenade, prompting a warning shot in return. Cambodia's Ministry of Information denied the claims, calling them 'fabricated'. The incident threatens the December truce that ended months of heavy fighting which displaced over a million people in 2025.
title: Thailand says troops exchanged fire at border, Cambodia denies ceasefire breach

summary: A major fire and multiple explosions occurred at a Thai Border Patrol Police ammunition depot in Surin province, roughly 50km from the border. The facility housed RPGs, mortar rounds, and rifle ammunition. While authorities suspect heat buildup as the cause, sabotage has not been ruled out. One officer was injured, and nearby housing was evacuated. Officials stressed there was no immediate cross-border risk.
title: Massive blast hits Thailand’s Border Patrol Police ammo depot in Surin

summary: Thai Army Chief Gen Pana Claewplodtook stated that while the military will not escalate the situation, Thailand plans to raise the recent border incident at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow is expected to address the 'distorted narratives' regarding the border row. The army believes the incident was caused by lack of discipline during a Cambodian troop rotation.
title: Thai Army responds cautiously to Cambodia's grenade attack; UN human rights intervention planned

summary: An ASEAN observation mission conducted between Feb 22-24 reported no major combat but confirmed limited troop movements and 2 km of new Thai barbed wire near Preah Vihear. The report notes that 150 hectares of Cambodian farmland remain inaccessible. Border trade has dropped significantly, with monthly losses estimated at $5 million due to semi-closed checkpoints at Doung, O'Smach, and Choam Sangke.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Border Tensions: From Ceasefire to Standoff

summary: In an interview in Brussels, Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized that Cambodia seeks de-escalation and peaceful coexistence with Thailand. He denied Thai accusations that Cambodian forces fired a grenade at a patrol on February 24. He also expressed concern over the 'fragile' nature of the border situation and claimed Thai forces have ventured beyond the frontier into areas Cambodia considers its sovereign territory.
title: Cambodia wants ‘de-escalation’ in conflict with Thailand, PM tells AFP

summary: In a rare international interview from Brussels, Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Cambodia seeks de-escalation and peaceful coexistence. He described the current border situation as 'not stable' and 'fragile,' noting that while Cambodia is ready to accept historical map surveys from France, Thai forces have allegedly ventured beyond established frontiers.
title: Cambodia wants 'deescalation' in conflict with Thailand: PM

summary: A new Migrant Worker Resource Centre (MRC) has opened in Siem Reap to assist returnees affected by the ongoing border conflict. The ILO reports that the center is timely due to the mass return of Cambodian workers from Thailand amid the instability, providing legal aid and reintegration services.
title: Cambodian migrant workers receive expanded support in Siem Reap province

summary: At the 61st Session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn accused Thailand of military expansion and human rights violations, stating the December ceasefire remains 'fragile.' Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow countered by highlighting online scam networks in Cambodia, which Thailand uses to justify its border posture, while denying territorial seizure.
title: Cambodia-Thailand border tensions spill onto the global stage at United Nations Human Rights Council

summary: Recent incidents, including the seizure of a Cambodian fishing boat and the alleged grenade fire in Sisaket, are straining the fragile peace. Cambodian officials state that liaison teams from both sides confirmed no weapons were fired by Khmer forces. The report notes that Thailand continues to occupy disputed territories with shipping containers and barbed wire, while Prime Minister Hun Manet seeks international arbitration through ASEAN and the UN.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Claims It Launched a Grenade at Thai Troops

summary: Human Rights Watch has condemned the 14-year prison sentences given to Cambodian journalists Phorn Sopheap and Pheap Pheara, who were charged with treason for reporting on the border conflict. The report also highlights the arrests of Meas Sara and Luot Sophal on incitement charges as part of a broader crackdown on freedom of speech since the conflict began.
title: Cambodian Journalists Unjustly Sentenced to 14 Years

summary: A Thai soldier was critically injured and lost his right leg after stepping on a landmine near the border in Surin province at dawn on Friday. The Thai military stated that a preliminary check suggests the mine was an older one buried deep in the ground, rather than a newly laid device. This incident occurs during a fragile ceasefire following heavy fighting in 2025 that displaced over a million people.
title: Thai soldier loses leg in landmine blast on Cambodia: Thailand military

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts issued a formal statement rejecting allegations that the UNESCO-listed Preah Vihear Temple has been used as a military base. The ministry emphasized its commitment to the 1954 Hague Convention, stating any security presence is strictly for protection.
title: Cambodia denies using Temple of Preah Vihear as military base in conflict

summary: The Thai caretaker government is convening the National Security Council to assess border risks. Tensions are high as political pressure mounts in Bangkok to cancel MOU 44, a maritime resource agreement. Analysts warn that scrapping the deal could lead to a new round of military confrontation.
title: Thai-Cambodia standoff risks flare-up with MOU 44 set for scrapping

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior reported that as of March 1, over 590,000 displaced people (92%) have returned to their homes following the December ceasefire. However, nearly 50,000 remain displaced, and essential services like schools and hospitals in Preah Vihear and Oddar Meanchey remain closed due to security concerns and ongoing monitoring of Thai military movements.
title: 92% of Displaced Border Residents Return Home, 49,352 Still Await Resettlement
